run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: Cart is down and everything that needs cart is failing. The cart pod cart-74587775fc-ndqmw (ReplicaSet cart-74587775fc) is in CrashLoopBackOff with 2 restarts and a last termination of exitCode 139 / reason Error, and its own log shows the fatal line 'Unhandled exception. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis' from cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected/Initialize. The cart Deployment therefore has no ready replicas, the cart Service (ClusterIP 10.96.19.17:8080) carries the pod only as notReadyAddresses, and callers get 'connect: connection refused'. Observed consequences on other services (each with its own error spans/logs): frontend GET/POST /api/cart and POST /api/checkout return 500, checkout PlaceOrder returns gRPC 13 INTERNAL 'cart failure: failed to get user cart during checkout', and frontend-proxy and load-generator record 500s. The deepest cause the evidence supports: the valkey-cart server running in pod valkey-cart-859985f49d-6sjb2 requires authentication - CONFIG GET returns requirepass with a (redacted) value, and INFO reports errorstat_NOAUTH count=1428 out of total_error_replies=1430 - while the cart container in Deployment cart has only VALKEY_ADDR in its env and no credentials, so the cart service crashes on its Redis connect check. The valkey-cart pod itself is Running/Ready with 0 restarts and low memory, and the Deployment spec has no command/args/env, so the auth requirement is in effect on the running server, not declared in that manifest; who applied it and when is unknown because change history is not integrated, hence conclusion partial. Checked and found healthy: probe_success=1 at 06:39:14 for ad, checkout, currency, email, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, payment, product-catalog, product-reviews, quote, recommendation, shipping (cart=0); no NetworkPolicies exist in the namespace; the Kafka cluster shows 1 broker, 0 offline partitions, 0 under-replicated partitions. Rejected as causes: OOM/memory pressure on cart (exit 139 not 137, container_oom_events_total=0, working set ~2.4MB vs 160Mi limit), flagd fault flags (every flag in ConfigMap flagd-config is at defaultVariant 'off', including cartFailure and failedReadinessProbe), NetworkPolicy blocking, and a Service selector mismatch (selector opentelemetry.io/name=cart matches the pod).

claims.text: Pod cart-74587775fc-ndqmw (namespace astronomy-shop, owner ReplicaSet cart-74587775fc) is Running but not ready: container cart has ready=false, restartCount=2, state waiting with reason CrashLoopBackOff, and lastState terminated reason Error with exitCode 139 (finished 2026-11-25T06:39:41Z); pod condition Ready=False reason ContainersNotReady.
The cart Deployment 'cart' has 1 desired/updated replica but no availableReplicas and no readyReplicas, i.e. zero ready replicas at 06:39:27Z.

The cart container log contains 'fail: cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore[0]' / 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' followed by 'Unhandled exception. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis' with stack frames at cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected (ValkeyCartStore.cs:line 101) and Initialize (line 71), timestamped 2026-11-25T06:39:07Z on pod cart-74587775fc-ndqmw.
The valkey-cart server has a password configured: CONFIG GET returns parameter requirepass with a redacted value (alongside masterauth/primaryauth, also redacted).

That server's INFO reports errorstat_NOAUTH count=1428 with total_error_replies=1430, total_connections_received=162 and total_commands_processed=84 - i.e. almost every error is an unauthenticated-client rejection; the same INFO shows uptime_in_seconds=133 at 06:40:11Z (process start ~06:37:58Z, matching the valkey-cart pod log 'Ready to accept connections' at 06:37:58Z).

Deployment valkey-cart (image valkey/valkey:9.0.1-alpine3.23, generation 1, last helm apply 06:37:28Z) declares no command, no args and no env; its pod valkey-cart-859985f49d-6sjb2 is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, so the password requirement is not declared in this manifest but is in effect on the running server.

The cart Deployment's container env contains VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379 (plus CART_PORT, ASPNETCORE_URLS, FLAGD_HOST/PORT, OTEL settings) and no Redis/Valkey password or secret reference; resources.limits.memory=160Mi; it defines no liveness or readiness probe.

Endpoints for Service cart (clusterIP 10.96.19.17, selector opentelemetry.io/name=cart) list the cart pod only under notReadyAddresses, so the ClusterIP has no ready backend; Endpoints for Service valkey-cart list pod valkey-cart-859985f49d-6sjb2 as a ready address on port 6379.

Frontend error spans (06:38:59-06:39:14Z) show oteldemo.CartService/GetCart and AddItem failing with rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and detail 'No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.19.17:8080', and GET/POST /api/cart plus POST /api/checkout returning http.status_code=500.

Checkout service error spans show oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder failing with rpc.grpc.status_code=13 and message 'cart failure: failed to get user cart during checkout: rpc error: code = Unavailable ... dial tcp 10.96.19.17:8080: connect: connection refused', with the child CartService/GetCart span at status code 14.

frontend-proxy spans ('router frontend egress', GET/POST) and load-generator spans (GET/POST, user_checkout_single) carry http.status_code=500 / error=true on the same traces that fail in frontend and checkout.

frontend pod frontend-6859c775df-qbhmf logs the same failure: 'Error: 13 INTERNAL: cart failure: failed to get user cart during checkout: ... dial tcp 10.96.19.17:8080: connect: connection refused' at 2026-11-25T06:39:03Z.

At 06:39:14Z blackbox probe_success{job="blackbox-astronomy-shop"} is 1 for ad, checkout, currency, email, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, payment, product-catalog, product-reviews, quote, recommendation and shipping, and 0 for cart; kafka.astronomy-shop:9092 is also 0 at every sampled point 06:37, 06:38 and 06:39Z.
The Kafka cluster is healthy at query time: 1 broker, 2 topics, 51 partitions, 0 offline partitions, 0 under-replicated partitions, no offline broker ids.
No NetworkPolicy objects exist in namespace astronomy-shop (0 objects returned), so pod-to-pod traffic between cart and valkey-cart is not filtered by policy.

Cart is not memory-starved: container_memory_working_set_bytes for the cart container is 2482176 bytes on pod cart-74587775fc-ndqmw (limit 160Mi) and container_oom_events_total for both cart pods is 0 at 06:39:14Z.

Every fault-injection flag in ConfigMap flagd-config is at defaultVariant 'off' (including cartFailure 'Fail cart service', failedReadinessProbe 'readiness probe failure for cart service', paymentFailure, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, emailMemoryLeak).

The previous cart pod cart-74587775fc-snq97 (same pod-template-hash 74587775fc, on node sregym-worker) logged a graceful 'Application is shutting down...' at 06:38:53Z and a kubelet event 'Stopping container cart' at 06:38:53Z; it had served AddItemAsync/GetCartAsync/EmptyCartAsync requests successfully at 06:38:38-06:38:47Z before being replaced by cart-74587775fc-ndqmw on node sregym-worker3.

The cart crash loop is caused by an authentication mismatch with its Valkey backend: the valkey-cart server requires a password (requirepass set, 1428 NOAUTH rejections) while the cart client supplies none (only VALKEY_ADDR in env), so ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected throws 'Wasn't able to connect to redis', the process exits (exitCode 139), the cart pod never becomes ready, and the cart ClusterIP refuses connections - which is the single upstream cause of the frontend /api/cart 500s and checkout PlaceOrder 'cart failure' errors.

The auth requirement was introduced at runtime on the already-running valkey-cart server (no restart: uptime confirms the process started 06:37:58Z and the pod has 0 restarts, while the earlier cart pod still completed cart operations at 06:38:38-06:38:47Z), most plausibly via a CONFIG SET / ACL change by an external actor around 06:38:48-06:38:54Z; the actor itself was not observed.

Cart crash-looping because of memory exhaustion/OOMKilled is rejected: last termination reason is Error with exitCode 139 (not 137/OOMKilled), container_oom_events_total is 0, and working set is ~2.4MB against a 160Mi limit.
A flagd-driven cart failure (flag cartFailure or failedReadinessProbe) is rejected: every flag in ConfigMap flagd-config, including both of those, is at defaultVariant 'off'.

A NetworkPolicy or Service-selector misconfiguration between frontend/checkout and cart is rejected: no NetworkPolicy objects exist in the namespace, Service cart selects opentelemetry.io/name=cart which matches the pod's labels, and its Endpoints contains that pod as a notReadyAddress rather than missing it.

Valkey-cart being down or unreachable as a server is rejected: its pod is Running and Ready with 0 restarts, its Endpoints address is ready, its process is up (uptime 133s, connected_clients 2, used_memory ~1.3MB, maxmemory 0) and it actively answers unauthenticated clients with NOAUTH errors.

Align authentication between cart and its backend: either clear the password on the valkey-cart server (e.g. CONFIG SET requirepass "" and persist the intended config) or supply the matching credential to the cart Deployment (env/secret) so ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected succeeds; then confirm the cart pod becomes Ready and the cart Service has a ready endpoint.

Track down the operator that mutated the running valkey-cart server config (requirepass) and the deletion of pod cart-74587775fc-snq97 around 06:38:50Z; enabling change-history/audit capture would make this attributable instead of inferred.

gaps: change_history is not integrated in this Run, so who applied the valkey-cart requirepass setting (and how: CONFIG SET vs ACL change) and who deleted pod cart-74587775fc-snq97 at 06:38:53Z could not be observed; the exact time the setting changed is inferred only from the last successful cart operations at 06:38:47Z and the first crash at 06:39:07Z.
The requirepass value is redacted by the Redis tool, so the password value could not be verified and no Secret could be read; whether cart was ever meant to send a matching credential is unverified.
Cart container logs after 06:39:14Z (the second/third crash at ~06:39:41Z) are outside the readable log window, so the later crash output was not read.

Queries for traces_span_metrics_calls_total / traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds (sum/count by service_name, instant and range over 06:09-06:39Z) returned nothing and get_series for that metric returned nothing, so no error-rate or latency series were available; SERIES ABSENT, not zero.

kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_exitcode and kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total at 06:39:14Z returned only the old pod cart-74587775fc-snq97 with 0 restarts (and no exitcode series), so the new pod's restart/exit counters are not observable in kube-state-metrics for this window.

probe_success for kafka.astronomy-shop:9092 is 0 at every sampled point (06:37, 06:38, 06:39Z) while the Kafka cluster itself reports 0 offline and 0 under-replicated partitions and no service was observed failing on Kafka; this discrepancy is unexplained and is not tied to the cart failures.

Error traces for the accounting service (06:38:30-06:39:14Z, tag error=true) returned no rows; only blackbox probe_success=1 was checked for services other than frontend, frontend-proxy, load-generator, checkout and cart, so their internal error rates were not verified.
Jaeger keeps only the most recent traces; trace data starts at 06:38:32Z, before that the onset of failures could not be traced.
next_steps: Inspect the valkey-cart server's ACL/users (ACL LIST/ACL CAT) and confirm whether requirepass was set deliberately; then re-align cart credentials with it.
Use an audit/change-history source (kube audit logs, chaos-injector logs) to identify the actor that set requirepass on valkey-cart and deleted cart-74587775fc-snq97.
After the credential fix, re-check cart pod readiness, Service cart endpoints, and frontend /api/cart error rate to confirm recovery.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
